newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arab Land Bank bond offer closing early.
newsitem.headline: Arab Land Bank bond offer closing early.

text.p: State-owned Arab Land Bank reported on Friday heavy demand for its seven-year floating-rate bonds worth 90 million pounds and said it would take the last subscriptions on Monday, the earliest date legally possible.
The bonds pay interest each six months at 1.5 percentage points below the Central Bank's discount rate, which has stood at 13.5 percent for the past 10 months.

"The Arab Land Bank bonds which it offered for subscription on August 31 have met with unprecedented demand... so the management of the Arab Land Bank has decided to close for subscriptions on Monday September 9," the bank said.
Under Egypt's capital market regulations, such issues must stay open for at least 10 days.
The Arab Land Bank bonds have been some of the most attractive on the Egyptian market in recent months.

Later this month the Egyptian treasury is offering seven-year bonds with a fixed yield of 11 percent and American Express Bank is offering five-year floating-rate notes linked to three-month treasury bills, which now yield 10.25 percent.
